questions.skill: Estimate the average rate of change of a function from its graph
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: The graph shows the distance d, in meters, that a cart has rolled after t seconds. Estimate the average rate of change from t = 1 to t = 3, with units.
questions.prompt_markup:
The graph shows the distance d, in meters, that a cart has rolled after t seconds.
Estimate the average rate of change from t = 1 to t = 3, with units.
questions.grading_note: Form required: an estimate with units. Accept 3.5 to 4.5 m/s: the graph passes about (1, 1) and (3, 9), and (9 - 1) ÷ 2 = 4.

questions.skill: Estimate the average rate of change of a function from its graph
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: The graph shows the distance d, in meters, that a cart has rolled after t seconds. Estimate the average rate of change from t = 3 to t = 5. Is the cart speeding up?
questions.prompt_markup:
The graph shows the distance d, in meters, that a cart has rolled after t seconds.
Estimate the average rate of change from t = 3 to t = 5. Is the cart speeding up?
questions.correct_answer: About 8 meters per second; yes, the rate is greater than on earlier intervals.
questions.grading_note: Form required: an estimate (7 to 9 m/s) and the conclusion. (25 - 9) ÷ 2 = 8.

questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: The average rate of change of d from t = 0 to t = 6 equals the slope of the segment joining (0, 0) and (6, 36) on the graph.
